reasoning_content: Wait — the fs-watcher detected test.wav on the initial scan (before the preset fix), and at that point the job failed. Does the watcher rescan the same file? The mtime change from touch should trigger it again. Let's monitor it.

action.command: cd /workspace/deployments/example-opencode && for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do sleep 30; echo "=== iter $i ==="; docker compose --env-file .env-example --env-file .env -f compose.yml -f compose.cpu.yml ps --format '{{.Name}}: {{.Status}}' 2>&1 | grep asr; docker compose --env-file .env-example --env-file .env -f compose.yml -f compose.cpu.yml logs --since 3m asr-service 2>&1 | tr '\r' '\n' | grep -viE "DEBUG|httpcore|GPUWatchdog|monitor|it/s|MB/s" | tail -6; echo "--- watch dir:"; ls -la watch/ | grep -vE "keep|jfk16k"; if ls watch/ 2>/dev/null | grep -qiE "\.txt$|Transkript|\.vtt$|\.srt$"; then echo "TRANSCRIPT FOUND!"; break; fi; done
